entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Octavius was a Roman senator who played a pivotal role in the tumultuous late Roman Republic. Elected consul alongside Lucius Cornelius Cinna in 87 BC, Octavius's fate was inextricably linked to the chaos that followed the capture of Rome by Cinna and Gaius Marius.

During the tumultuous years leading up to the assassination of Cinna, Octavius worked closely with other prominent figures, including Marius and the Roman general Sulla. His actions were driven by a desire to restore stability and order to the Republic, a goal that would ultimately prove elusive.

Despite his efforts, Octavius's legacy was marked by tragedy. His own life was cut short, and he died during the tumultuous period that followed Cinna's assassination.

The impact of Octavius's actions was felt long after his death. His efforts to stabilize the Republic paved the way for the eventual rise of the Roman Empire under Augustus, one of his adopted sons.

As a testament to the enduring power of the Roman Republic, Octavius's legacy continues to captivate historians and scholars today.

The 86 BCE assassination of Gnaeus Octavius remains a pivotal moment in Roman history, one that marked the end of an era and the beginning of a new chapter in the Republic's tumultuous history.
